identity.name: ASARFI HOSPITAL LIMITED
identity.industry: Regional Private Hospitals & Oncology Care (Eastern India)

summary.oneLiner: Asarfi Hospital delivered robust FY26 growth (Rev +42%, PAT +58%) driven by volume ramp-up in its super-specialty unit and scaling cancer hospital, with FY27 guidance targeting INR 260 Cr revenue supported by bed expansion and imminent inorganic acquisition. Key value unlock lies in migrating to the main board and resolving regulatory delays for bone marrow transplants to capture underserved oncology demand in Jharkhand.

one-line thesis: Asarfi Hospital delivered robust FY26 growth (Rev +42%, PAT +58%) driven by volume ramp-up in its super-specialty unit and scaling cancer hospital, with FY27 guidance targeting INR 260 Cr revenue supported by bed expansion and imminent inorganic acquisition. Key value unlock lies in migrating to the main board and resolving regulatory delays for bone marrow transplants to capture underserved oncology demand in Jharkhand.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 173.5 Cr (+42% YoY); EBITDA: INR 35.3 Cr (+42% YoY), Margin 20% (down from ~20.5% implied); PAT: INR 16.7 Cr (+58% YoY), Margin 10%; Q4 Rev: INR 45.2 Cr (+29% YoY), EBITDA INR 7.7 Cr (17% margin); Order Book: N/A (Service sector); Net Debt: Near zero (Cash INR 8-10 Cr, Capex funded via accruals); One-offs: Prior year 'Other Income' of INR 3.66 Cr not repeated in FY26.
guidance: FY27 Revenue: INR 260 Cr; EBITDA Margin: 22% (stepping stone to 23-25% by FY28); PAT Margin: 13-15%; Capex: <INR 15 Cr (INR 8-10 Cr for Research Institute, INR 2-3 Cr for cancer bed expansion); Bed Capacity: Scale cancer unit from 65 to 150 beds.
order book & pipeline: N/A for hospital services; however, visible growth pipeline includes 85 new cancer beds, bone marrow transplant unit (pending approval), and one near-finalized hospital acquisition.
segment / subsidiary detail: Super Specialty: 285 beds, ARPOB INR 23,000, surgeries +26% YoY (>6,300); Cancer Hospital: 65 beds, occupancy 42%, Rev INR 33 Cr (+65% YoY), contributes 10-12% of total revenue, Ayushman Bharat mix ~15% of cancer rev.
growth verticals / optionality: 1) Cancer hospital bed expansion (65 to 150 beds) with low capex intensity; 2) Bone marrow transplant unit launch (delayed 4-5 months due to state policy); 3) Inorganic acquisition of one hospital (technical issues being resolved); 4) Management contracts in neighboring districts.
margins & cost dynamics: FY26 EBITDA margin at 20%; Q4 margin compressed to 17% due to case-mix and government scheme delays; Targeting 22% in FY27 via better case-mix (patients from 10 neighboring districts) and cost control; long-term target 23-25%.
capex / expansion: FY27 Capex guidance <INR 15 Cr: INR 8-10 Cr for Healthcare Management Research Institute; INR 2-3 Cr for cancer hospital bed expansion (65 to 150 beds); funded largely through internal accruals, though debt optionality exists for large opportunities.
capital allocation: Prioritizing organic expansion (cancer beds, research institute) and near-term inorganic acquisition via internal accruals (Cash: INR 8-10 Cr); Open to debt for strategic opportunities; No dividend mentioned, reinvestment mode.
risks & watch-items: 1) Regulatory delays (Bone marrow transplant approval stalled due to Jharkhand state policy); 2) Government scheme reimbursement delays impacting cash flows (Ayushman Bharat/state schemes); 3) Political uncertainty affecting scheme approvals; 4) Execution risk on aggressive FY27 guidance (+50% growth implied).
management quality / tone: Optimistic and aggressive on growth targets; transparent about regulatory bottlenecks (transplant policy, merger heirship issues); confident on main board migration post-July 2026; defensive on receivable aging (6-7 months) but claiming improvement.
non-obvious takeaways: Cancer hospital ARPOB volatility in Q4 was driven by administrative approval delays in state schemes rather than demand destruction; The 'merger' delay is specific to inheritance issues of deceased shareholders in the target entity, not valuation disputes; Only 3 dedicated cancer hospitals exist in entire Jharkhand (<500 total oncology beds), creating a near-monopoly dynamic for Asarfi in the region.

themes.title: Hospitals, diagnostics & domestic healthcare
themes.need: Under-bedded India plus insurance penetration and preventive-care adoption drive a domestic healthcare capex + volume cycle distinct from export pharma. MAXHEALTH adding ~2,500+ beds (Gurgaon 500-bed by FY27); APOLLOHOSP/MEDANTA/KIMS/NH/ASTERDM/MAXHEALTH on hospitals; LALPATHLAB/METROPOLIS/THYROCARE/VIJAYA on diagnostics (LALPATHLAB guides 13-15% FY27); MEDPLUS/ENTERO on pharmacy/distribution; POLYMED on devices. The same India-only demand engine now also carries India-facing branded pharma, which is driven by domestic volume and price rather than the export book: GLAXO delivered its first INR 1,000cr quarter with 8.1% revenue growth, Shingrix at a ~INR 75cr annual run-rate (CY25, +80% YoY) and Jemperli's first-line approval expanding eligible patients from 800 to 6,000; ERIS (dermatology 15% of revenue after INR 1,265cr of domestic brand acquisitions), SANOFI (India-for-India, NLEM price cuts) and THEMISMED (hospital segment +20% YoY) sit on the same axis.
themes.driver: New-bed commissioning + occupancy ramp; Tier 3/4 diagnostics penetration; CGHS rate revision; preventive-test volumes; domestic branded-formulation volume growth and NLEM/price actions.
